fix(pricing): the table is asked for once a held record has an entry no cost priced (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.wi3)

A machine whose transcripts all carry costUSD reads no table, so its
statusline tick starts no fetch of pricing.json and, offline, warns of no
table it never priced by. The ask stays in the request's refresh, the one
effect per tick; a record a scan holds with unpriced tokens makes the next
request ask, since today prices it by the table.
fix(pricing): a day's disk copy does not replace a newer table this owner holds (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.wi3)
fix(pricing): an empty entry model names no model, so the message's model prices the entry (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.wi3)

fix(pricing): the table is derived by landing, the load latch opens however the load ends (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.wi3)

From the high review of PR #691:

- A derivation over the table moves only when a table does: the landing is
  a computed told apart by its moment, so a retry that lands nothing, or a
  refresh that finds the day's copy on disk, recomputes nothing downstream.
  Pinned by a test that fails under reference equality.
- The one-load latch is released in a finally, so a load that rejects
  cannot leave the daemon on the bundled rates for its whole life.
- The parse's token and raw shapes are interfaces: the exception that kept
  them aliases named a boundary this PR tightened away.
- The merge of a session's file folds is a FileFold, not a second type of
  the same shape.
- The token total is one function on the breakdown's module, in place of
  three hand sums.

fix(pricing): entries folded before the table landed are priced by it when it lands (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.wi3)

A fold priced each un-costed entry with the table held when it ran and
stored the sum, so a daemon that started offline kept the bundled rates
for every entry folded before the live table landed, in the session total
and in today, until a rewrite re-folded the file from zero.

A record now holds the price's inputs and no price: the cost its entries
carried themselves, and the tokens of the entries that carried none by
the model they are priced as. Every reader prices the record with the
table held at the read. The pricing adapter's table is an observable
read, and the ask that starts a due load is a separate effect the
request's refresh makes, so the day sums and the session draw recompute
in the turn a table lands and no read inside a derivation starts a load.
Nothing waits for the first load any more: a cold daemon's first frame
draws at the bundled rates and is re-priced when the table lands.

Tests: a store over the live adapter and the mocked network folds entries
before the fetch answers and reads the landed table's price for them
after it, with no transcript read and no refresh, and again when the
day's table lands; a carried cost stands under any table; the adapter's
cases are restated over the read and the ask, with a reaction observing
the landing.

test(facts): the live request states its deadline from the instant it arrives, crosses the checkpoint before the setup's burn, and the header names the whole request path (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.izh)
test(facts): the live session states a client's deadline, spells its argv once, and checks the pane its checkpoint stamped (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.izh)

test(facts): the live session's request crosses the render checkpoint and the daemon's render setup (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.izh)

The live session in facts-seam built its request by hand and cast it to
a checked request, leaving out the deadline, encoding, rate limits,
requested origin and the pane's start time, and built its render setup by
hand beside the daemon's. It now sends the wire request a client run by
Claude Code's pid 4242 sends, crosses checkRenderRequest with the daemon's
own parts, and draws the setup setUpRender returns: the pane is stamped
from the Claude Code record the case lays down, and no cast or hand-built
setup remains.

fix(update-act): a spend fault holds between looks, and the end's wording is spelled once

Medium review of PR #694:
- The spend look's fault is the watch's own value, set at each look, not
  touchActs' read fault: a successful read between ticks (the restart hold's
  running(), or act()) cleared it and the ⚠ blinked off.
- An unreadable spend's fault no longer names where the look counted from,
  which moved after the first look and made one fault read as two.
- What the end did to the group is spelled once; the unrecorded reason is
  the logged line.
- The header says the act's files outrank the daemon's copy once they hold
  a larger spend, as latestLook ranks.

brandon-unfiled-3248.7cay

fix(update-act): a fault reads the same at every look, a failed read keeps the shared spend, and cleanup never blocks an end (brandon-unfiled-3248.7cay)

High review of PR #694:
- A write fault names the published file and the errno code, not the
  message that names a fresh staged path each look, so the change logger
  dedupes it and the warning text holds still.
- A spend file that can't be read is left in place and the look counts on
  from this daemon's own; only bytes that can't be parsed are replaced, so a
  transient read error no longer hands the act a fresh budget.
- The latest look is the larger spend, ties going to the later look: a wall
  clock set back no longer lets a stale copy win.
- A staging is removed only when it is there: in a directory that can't be
  searched the removal's EACCES replaced the verdict and nothing was ended.
- An act whose files vanish before its end is logged, with its pid.
- The unrecorded-end reason is keyed by job, not act number, and
  error() reads it directly.
- The verdict write's type is the one JobEnding derives from; the warning
  prefix is spelled once.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(update-act): an act whose files can't be written is still ended after its budget (brandon-unfiled-3248.7cay)

A look now judges its spend before it reports a write it could not make:
spendLook returns the spend and its fault instead of throwing, and counts
on from the later of the act's files and this daemon's own last look of
the same job (the reader's job identity decides "same job"). endJob
signals the group even when its timeout verdict can't be written, as a
new `unrecorded` arm of JobEnding, and the watch keeps why it ended that
act so the warning still says so once the group is gone.

fix(colour)!: the door's ✖ is a red at every depth, chosen as the depth draws it (brandon-unfiled-3248.7u1g)

At ansi the open settings door's ✖ was drawn silver, yellow, purple or
black: the red was chosen as truecolor measures it, and keptOn's repair
searched the depth's table by contrast alone. The choice now measures
every candidate and the ground as the render's depth draws them, and
the candidates are per depth: the theme's named reds in truecolor and
at 256 colours, the terminal's red and bright red (SGR 31/91) at ansi.
keptOn has no job left and is deleted.

BREAKING CHANGE: the keptOn template function is removed (use
readableOn fg bg ratio instead), and roleTextOn accepts only the
semantic roles error, warning and success.

fix(watchers): the daemon probes birth time at boot, in its state directory, and builds its disk over the verdict (brandon-unfiled-3248.0463)

The probe ran ambiently on any process's first stat, on the real clock and
in the spawning shell's TMPDIR, behind two disabled lint rules. A process
main now probes once with its own clock in a folder it owns, logs the
verdict (warn when unprobed), and hands the daemon a disk built over it; no
CLI process or client tick pays for a probe. Jest's global hooks resolve a
`.js` specifier to its TypeScript source as a test's registry does, so src
keeps one import spelling.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(watchers): a folder's identity stays put across child writes where birth time is a ctime copy (brandon-unfiled-3248.0463)

Where statx fails, libuv copies ctime into birth time for the life of the
process, and a directory's ctime moves on every child create, remove or
rename, so every write in a watched folder read as another folder. The
disk adapter now probes once per process, on its first stat, whether birth
time moves with ctime, and Stat and FolderIdentity carry no birth time
(null) where the host copies ctime or statx reports 0. The daemon logs the
verdict at startup.

fix(daemon): a connection's state is one value, and past waiting it reads no more frames (#689)

* fix(daemon): a connection's state is one value, and past waiting it reads no more frames (brandon-unfiled-3248.df7i)

A connection's lifecycle is one state (awaiting, answering, unattended,
answered, held, streaming, closed) moved by one pure transition table; the
connection only performs the effects a step names. In-flight and the
backstop are columns of the table, so each moves once, on crossing its line.

A connection reads exactly one frame: a second frame, a frame after the
answer, and the bytes behind an over-cap header or unparseable frame are
never handled or buffered. A reply that cannot be encoded is answered
RENDER_FAILED and ends the stream, its exit still sequenced on that flush.
A dropped exit's warning names its one cause: the client was told TIMEOUT.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(daemon): a url frame read past the deadline stays unattended, a socket error is the peer leaving, and a frame handler's throw is heard (brandon-unfiled-3248.df7i)

- The read carries who waits in every state: a url frame read after the
  backstop answered is unattended and lapsed, so its forwarder's hang-up
  no longer leaves in-flight or reads as a client gone mid-click.
- A socket error moves the state to closed, so a click whose turn falls
  between the destroy and the 'close' sees its client gone.
- readOneFrame delivers its first outcome outside the reader's parse, so a
  throw from onFrame reaches the stream instead of being dropped as a
  second parse failure.
- The connection uses reply.ts's stay-up reply instead of a copy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(daemon): a frame handler's synchronous throw is answered RENDER_FAILED, never an exception out of the socket's read (brandon-unfiled-3248.df7i)

The connection's frame handling runs inside one promise started in the
read's turn, so a throw before its first await takes the handler-threw
path. readOneFrame raising onFrame's throw would otherwise end the shared
daemon through uncaughtException.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(daemon): a subscription the feed took after the connection moved on is ended, not dropped (brandon-unfiled-3248.df7i)

The subscribed cell unsubscribes from every state but answering, so the
table no longer depends on nothing interleaving with the feed's
subscribe. The connection builds a reply event through reply.ts's
replied, and the clientLeft comment says when a url frame's writer
counts as present.

fix(git): each session's git reads answer for its own directory (brandon-unfiled-3248.i3ek)

A daemon spawned from an environment carrying GIT_DIR or another of git's
repository variables (a hook, vcsh, yadm) passed it to every git read, so
every bar showed the spawning shell's repository. The daemon now asks git
for those names once at its process edge, before its lease, bounded at 2 s,
and runs in a world whose environment is the process's without them. An ask
that fails keeps the inherited environment and draws a git-env warning on
every bar; a git that is not installed names none.

fix(cache): each catch-up turn takes the most recently used due entry as the map stands (candybar-animation-wbxz.v24)

A session drawn during the walk is now re-read on the next turn, not
where its entry stood when the batch began. A turn clears its handle
before it reloads and arms only when none is armed, so a batch started
inside a turn leaves one walker. A throw is logged with its stack.

fix(cache): a catch-up turn is its own error boundary and walks most recently used first (candybar-animation-wbxz.v24)

A walk turn runs from setImmediate, outside the watcher registry's
try/catch, so a reload that threw there reached uncaughtException and
shut the daemon down. The turn now logs the throw and arms the next.

The walk takes the most recently used entry first, so the bar in front
of the user is re-read on the first turn. The due set is a Set: every
due entry always reloads for the latest batch's cause, which the armed
turn carries.

fix(cache): a catch-up reloads one entry per turn, so requests are answered between entries (candybar-animation-wbxz.v24)

When file events resumed after a stall, or the repo answers moved, the
render cache reloaded every entry in one synchronous turn. A reload that
keeps its state still resolves, validates and keys the whole chain, so
105 entries held the live daemon's loop for 1.7s on a calm machine and
11s on a loaded one, and every client waiting behind it hung up (the
EPIPE bursts in daemon.log).

The walk now takes one due entry per turn of the loop. Any reload clears
its entry's due mark, a drop clears a dropped entry's, a reload that
throws ends only its own turn, and close cancels the armed turn. The
render cache's stats count the entries still due.
Merge 9cfce78aed5fb0edc8a096e2bb32236ce4bc81e0 into d8be82f47dab2890d335b8563bbfdc937aedba77

fix(config): undo puts a click's text back on the disk the click wrote; a write's stat error is never a cleanup's (candybar-testing-ihvy.5zt)

- The settings history takes the daemon's disk, and the config text read and
  write take a disk: a click, its proof, its write and its undo are one
  disk's. config-file-store leaves the systemFilesystem owners.
- writeAtomicOn takes the replaced file's mode before the tmp exists, so a
  stat that fails is the error the caller sees.
- config.md: ENOTDIR counts as absent beside ENOENT.

fix(config): a click writes its home on the disk it read and proved; the book's folder is absent as presence says (candybar-testing-ihvy.5zt)

- ConfigHome carries the click's writable disk; the commit writes through it
  (writeAtomicOn), so a click's read, proof and write are one disk's. Undo
  keeps its own system-disk pair until the settings history takes a disk.
- bookIsFiled asks presence(): a book folder that is a regular file holds no
  book, and the loose book is read.
- holdsGit asks presence() and marks its no-silent-failure exception; the
  ascent carrying the failure is candybar-testing-ihvy.izc.sv9.

fix(config): a click's proof shares the render cache's installed layers and reads its home's disk (candybar-testing-ihvy.5zt)

- ConfigHome carries the installed-layer memo its loads share; the render
  cache lends its own through the verb context, so a click's proof checks no
  plugin the bar's last load already checked. The memo keys on definition
  text, so a lent memo serves no layer the borrower's disk does not hold.
- presence() reads ENOTDIR as absent, as the stat it replaced did: a path
  through a regular file holds nothing. The filesystem contract pins ENOTDIR.
- A click reads its home's text and the layers above on the disk its proof
  loads; config-file-store leaves FS_READERS.
- The lane edge's fileExists asks the same disk as its presence.
- stateFromLoad folds into loadFromDisk; keyLoad is module-private.

feat(config): a renderer loads config as a value over the filesystem port (candybar-testing-ihvy.5zt)

Every read a config load makes goes through the FilesystemReads it is
handed: the answers book, discovery, worktree links, plugin folders, each
layer and each definition. readConfigLoad (src/config/load.ts) is the load
as a value; the render cache builds state from it. Each definition is read
once per load, and the installed-plugin memo is an owned value keyed on
the texts, not module state keyed on a stat. The answers book's read moves
into Config, the state-file store into src/disk. Repo-approval cases move
to test/unit over the fake. Ten files leave FS_READERS; Config gets an
import rule.
